title: Left fibrations preserve right-anodyne maps under base change
statement:
Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns and degreewise pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], left fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and right anodyne maps of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. Work in any fixed containing universe. Let $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be a right anodyne map of simplicial sets, and let $q:Z\to Y$ be a left fibration, meaning that $q$ lifts every horn $\Lambda_j^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq j<n$. Then the pullback inclusion
$$X\times_Y Z\longrightarrow Z$$
is right anodyne. Neither $Y$ nor $Z$ is assumed to be a quasicategory. A right anodyne map here belongs to the class generated by the inclusions $\Lambda_j^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, $0<j\leq n$, and isomorphisms under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.11, printed p.159 (PDF p.174, zero-based), with Proposition 4.4.4(iv), printed p.156, unpacking properness as preservation of right-anodyne inclusions under pullback. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial one-sided-fibration theorem.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C$ be the class of monomorphisms $a:A\hookrightarrow B$ whose pullback along every left fibration $E\to B$ is right anodyne. A pullback of a left fibration is a left fibration: project a horn lifting problem to the original map, fill it there, and pair the filler with its prescribed base simplex. Pullback in simplicial sets commutes with colimits in a slice: degreewise, an element of a colimit has a representative over a fixed base element, and all identifications stay in that fiber. Thus pulling back a pushout or a continuous ordinal chain gives the pushout or chain of the pulled-back maps. For the pushout $S=B\amalg_A A_1$ of $a:A\hookrightarrow B$ along $A\to A_1$, and a left fibration $E\to S$, the pullback inclusion $A_1\times_S E\hookrightarrow E$ is the pushout of $A\times_S E\hookrightarrow B\times_S E$ along $A\times_S E\to A_1\times_S E$. The map $B\times_S E\to B$ is a left fibration, so the attaching inclusion is right anodyne if $a\in\mathcal C$. For a continuous chain $B_0\to B_\theta$, pull a left fibration $E\to B_\theta$ back to each $B_\alpha$; each successor pullback is right anodyne by membership of the corresponding successor in $\mathcal C$, and the pulled-back chain is continuous by the degreewise calculation. Thus $\mathcal C$ is closed under pushouts and small transfinite compositions. For an arrow retract of $a:A\to B$ from $b:A'\to B'$, write the section maps as $u:A\to A'$, $s:B\to B'$ and the retraction maps as $v:A'\to A$, $r:B'\to B$, so $bu=sa$, $av=rb$, $vu=1$ and $rs=1$. Given a left fibration $p:E\to B$, pull it back along $r$ to $E'=B'\times_B E\to B'$. Under the identification $A'\times_{B'}E'=A'\times_B E$, the pulled-back source section and retraction are $(x,e)\mapsto(u(x),e)$ and $(x',e)\mapsto(v(x'),e)$, and the codomain maps are $e\mapsto(s(p(e)),e)$ and $(y',e)\mapsto e$. Their squares commute by $bu=sa$ and $av=rb$, and their composites are identities by $vu=1$ and $rs=1$. The pullback of $a$ is therefore an arrow retract of the right-anodyne pullback of $b$. Hence $\mathcal C$ is retract-closed and contains all isomorphisms. All these assertions are degreewise set constructions and retain the simplicial operators.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.11, first paragraph: saturation of the class C; explicit expansion by the worker, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The class $\mathcal C$ has right cancellation among monomorphisms. Indeed let $f:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $g:B\hookrightarrow C$ satisfy $f,gf\in\mathcal C$, and take any left fibration $E\to C$. Set $E_B=B\times_C E$ and $E_A=A\times_C E$. The maps $E_A\hookrightarrow E_B$ and $E_A\hookrightarrow E$ are right anodyne by the definition of $\mathcal C$ and Step 1. All three inclusion maps are monomorphisms. Apply [lem-coef-right-anodyne-mono-cancellation] to conclude that $E_B\hookrightarrow E$ is right anodyne. This proves $g\in\mathcal C$.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.11, first paragraph, using Corollary 4.1.10; explicit expansion by the worker, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: We will lift relative initial prisms against left fibrations. For a monomorphism $K\hookrightarrow L$, put $D_0=(\{0\}\times L)\cup(\Delta^1\times K)$. Reverse simplex order as follows: for $\alpha:[a]\to[b]$, put $\bar\alpha(j)=b-\alpha(a-j)$; let $S^{\mathrm{op}}_a=S_a$ with operators induced by $\bar\alpha$. This involution preserves products, unions, pushouts, continuous ordinal chains and arrow retracts degreewise. It identifies the opposite of the $i$th horn of dimension $n$ with the $(n-i)$th horn, and swaps the endpoints of $\Delta^1$. Consequently the opposite of $D_0\hookrightarrow\Delta^1\times L$ is the pushout-product of the right horn $\{1\}=\Lambda_1^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ with $K^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow L^{\mathrm{op}}$. By [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product] it is right anodyne. A left fibration, after this involution, lifts all right horns by its defining lifting condition. It lifts their pushouts by the attaching square, their transfinite composites by [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting], and their arrow retracts by composing the section, filler and retraction squares. Undoing the involution proves that every left fibration lifts $D_0\hookrightarrow\Delta^1\times L$.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.11, final paragraph: the relative homotopy lift, expanded using the opposite of Proposition 3.4.3; explicit expansion by the worker, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix any simplicial set $T$ and a left fibration $p:E\to\Delta^1\times T$. Let $K=E\times_{\Delta^1}\{1\}$ and $i:K\hookrightarrow E$. The monotone function $\max:[1]\times[1]\to[1]$ defines a simplicial map and hence a base homotopy $b:\Delta^1\times E\to\Delta^1\times T$ with $b(t,e)=(\max(t,s(e)),y(e))$, where $p(e)=(s(e),y(e))$. On $\{0\}\times E$ prescribe the lift $e\mapsto e$, and on $\Delta^1\times K$ prescribe $(t,k)\mapsto i(k)$. They agree on the intersection and lie over $b$, since $\max(t,1)=1$. Step 3 supplies a lift $H:\Delta^1\times E\to E$ extending both. Its endpoint $H(1,-)$ lands in $K$, because its first base coordinate is 1; denote the induced map by $r:E\to K$. Then $ri=1_K$, $H(0,-)=1_E$, $H(1,-)=ir$, and $H(t,i(k))=i(k)$ exactly. No filler or homotopy is taken in a quasicategory; all lifts are horn lifts for $p$.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.11, last paragraph: explicit lifted max homotopy; explicit expansion by the worker, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $D_1=(\Delta^1\times K)\cup(\{1\}\times E)\subseteq\Delta^1\times E$. The inclusion $u:D_1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1\times E$ is right anodyne by [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], applied to $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and the monomorphism $i:K\hookrightarrow E$. The homotopy $H$ of Step 4 sends $D_1$ into $i(K)$: it is $i(k)$ on the first part and $ir(e)$ on the second. Let $k:D_1\to K$ be the induced restriction. In the arrow category, maps from $i$ to $u$ are $k_0:K\to D_1$, $k_0(x)=(0,i(x))$, and $e_0:E\to\Delta^1\times E$, $e_0(e)=(0,e)$; maps back are $k$ and $H$. The squares commute, $kk_0=1_K$, and $He_0=1_E$. Thus $i$ is an arrow retract of $u$ and is right anodyne. Since $p$ was arbitrary, the endpoint inclusion $e_T:\{1\}\times T\hookrightarrow\Delta^1\times T$ belongs to $\mathcal C$ for every $T$, including the empty simplicial set.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.10 and Proposition 4.4.11: explicit arrow retract; explicit expansion by the worker, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For every monomorphism $a:A\hookrightarrow B$, the relative final prism $P(a):D=(\Delta^1\times A)\cup(\{1\}\times B)\hookrightarrow\Delta^1\times B$ belongs to $\mathcal C$. In fact $j:\{1\}\times B\hookrightarrow D$ is the pushout of $e_A$ along $\{1\}\times a$, so Step 1 and Step 5 give $j\in\mathcal C$. The composite $P(a)j=e_B$ also belongs to $\mathcal C$. All maps are degreewise injections. Right cancellation from Step 2 now gives $P(a)\in\mathcal C$. This uses only the already established properties of $\mathcal C$, not a claim that all right-anodyne pullbacks are known yet.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.11, reduction via Lemma 3.1.3: spelled-out pushout and cancellation; explicit expansion by the worker, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$ and $0<k\leq n$, and put $A=\Lambda_k^n$, $B=\Delta^n$. The horn inclusion $a:A\hookrightarrow B$ is an arrow retract of $P(a)$. On vertex posets define monotone maps $s:[n]\to[1]\times[n]$ by $s(v)=(0,v)$ for $v<k$ and $s(v)=(1,v)$ for $v\geq k$, and $r:[1]\times[n]\to[n]$ by $r(0,v)=\min(v,k)$, $r(1,v)=\max(v,k)$. Both branches of $r$ are monotone in $v$, and for $v\leq w$ across branches, $\min(v,k)\leq k\leq\max(w,k)$; $s$ is monotone since its first coordinate changes only from 0 to 1. Applying these formulas to each entry of a simplex gives simplicial maps commuting with precomposition, with $rs=1_B$. The second coordinate of $s$ is the identity, so $s(A)\subseteq\Delta^1\times A\subseteq D$. On $\{1\}\times B$, the image of $r$ misses vertex 0 because $k>0$, hence is in $A$. For a simplex of $\Delta^1\times A$, its second-coordinate image misses some vertex $v\ne k$. Every value of its image under $r$ is either its second-coordinate value or $k$, so it still misses $v$ and lies in $A$. Thus $r(D)\subseteq A$, and the restrictions of $s,r$ to $A,D$ together with $s,r$ on $B,\Delta^1\times B$ give section and retraction squares for $a$ and $P(a)$. Step 6 and retract closure therefore put every right horn in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.3, first half of proof: explicit horn retract, used in Proposition 4.4.11; explicit expansion by the worker, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Steps 1 and 7 show that $\mathcal C$ contains the isomorphisms and right horn inclusions and is closed under pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts. The defining minimality of the right-anodyne class [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne] implies that every right-anodyne $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ is in $\mathcal C$. Applying this membership to the specified left fibration $q:Z\to Y$ gives $X\times_Y Z\hookrightarrow Z$ right anodyne, as required. All objects and ordinal chains stay in the fixed containing universe; no Kan or quasicategory assumption was used.
